utterances.text: Here the Prosecution showed you images from Van Lynden. I'd like to show you a document. I can't find the page right now. Van Lynden said that these clips had been put together, it wasn't a direct broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 3 in both the Serbian and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes from the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina of the 17th of June, 1992. What important event took place on that date, on the 17th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th of June, if my memory doesn't fail me, around that time we liberated the Zlatiste-Pale road. It was around the 16th or 17th. I don't remember what happened exactly. I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at what Halilovic says, please. I see that Halilovic is talking about Sarajevo. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a bit, please. It's difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the situation that Halilovic describes?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Halilovic was the head, the chief, of the Muslim General Staff or Main Staff, Sefer Halilovic, if we're talking about him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 6 in the Serbian version and page 5 in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What we have in yellow is what I'll read out. This is what Halilovic said, his conclusions about Sarajevo. "In the course of a two-month period of activity, the aggressor sustained a lot of losses in manpower and especially in terms of equipment lost. He lost about 20 tanks, 20 personnel carriers, six multiple-rocket launchers, five howitzers, seven 120-millimetre mortars and there was a certain number -- a certain amount of equipment was lost and burned, three tanks, six armoured carriers, five howitzers 155-millimetre ones, six mortars, and a significant amount of infantry weapons. Because of important losses in terms of equipment, the intensity of artillery and rocket attacks on Sarajevo diminished." Who inflicted these losses on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only the Muslim forces could have done that. If we're talking about the Sarajevo battle-field anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Under 2, a bit lower down, five, six lines lower down: "The disposition of forces of the TO in the Sarajevo region, the Territorial Defence region of Sarajevo, consists of the following: The regional TO staff in the Sarajevo region, two 120-millimetre batteries, 12 pieces; 105-millimetre howitzer batteries, five pieces; an artillery platoon that consists of three pieces of 122-millimetre pieces; an armoured mechanised platoon, or rather, a group; one tank; and five armoured carriers; 16 TO staffs, municipal staffs; 16 TO detachments; about 500 independent platoons; about 450 independent companies; and about 100 anti-sabotage platoons." Did you know anything about the forces facing you, the SRK, from the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, we were well aware of that and that is why we defended ourselves. We mounted a decisive defence at our positions. It is a fact that they weren't as empty-handed as it was said and this can be seen from the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see page 11 in the Serbian version and then page 10 in the English version which continues on page 11 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the lower part it says that 91.720 individuals who are registered, 95 were armed, defence is resisting, significant objectives were attained, Chetnik forces in Pofalici, Zuc, and Mojmilo were routed. In the last few days of the war there were significant successes by the artillery units when mounting a defence of the town of Sarajevo. Thank you. Was it necessary to tell -- was it possible to say whose artillery was concerned in Van Lynden's images?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I couldn't tell whose artillery it was, whose artillery was opening fire. On the basis of this document, one can see that at the time they were well armed and equipped with artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 1D20069, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about Stari Grad, the old part of town here. Bascarsija is perhaps what one had in mind. Please have a look at this, the Municipal Assembly of the armed forces, Stari Grad, the 16th of July, 1992. Under 2: "The units of the Stari Grad OS participated in the liberation and capturing of the Bistricka Kula facility which is a dominant feature. We are working on engineering fortification of the position at this facility and on all the other defence lines." And then further down: "Action is being taken to establish new units, for example, the Stari Grad Brigade and the already-existing units are to become part of this brigade." My question, Colonel, is as follows: Could you tell us without me reminding you of the fact which brigades there were once the war had broken out, which brigades there were or which brigades were deployed in Stari Grad, in fact?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, unfortunately I can't remember, I really can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the 105th Muslim Brigade was deployed?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have really forgotten everything. It's been over 20 years since these events, and I haven't been involved in these issues, I wanted to get everything as soon as possible, so I have forgotten many things and I could not confirm where certain brigades were, in fact, deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It would be leading if I said that the 105th and the 115th were in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, it would be and I don't think --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking for a response. I'm not asking for a response. Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In general terms and in principle, the document you have just seen, how does this document tally with what you know about the arms that the people in Stari Grad had?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows that in all parts of the city their units were deployed by establishment as they had them. They were equipped with equipment and manpower. They were better equipped and had more manpower than we had.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this now be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2414, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to call up P847.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The document has already been shown to you, it was shown to you earlier today as well. Could you please look at bullet point 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this part below bullet point 2 be zoomed in? It says here: "If a cease-fire agreement is signed, the artillery weapons should be moved further away from Sarajevo ..." and so on and so forth. A ban on moving weapons and military positions and so on and so forth. Bullet point 3: "As long as there is a threat of NATO air-strikes against our forces, do not turn the infantry, artillery, and OMJ away from the Muslims and UNPROFOR and do everything to maintain direct contact including full fortification."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, Colonel, sir, what were the circumstances when General Milovanovic issued this order and how does the cover-up of weapons and air-strikes correspond to each other?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was when NATO air-strikes and rapid reaction artillery were active against the VRS. The order was issued in order to be as close and in -- in direct contact with Muslim forces in order to preserve manpower and equipment because we knew that they wouldn't strike if we were close to Muslim positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to call up 1D03408.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked, Colonel, sir, about the number of shells and about the proportionality of response. I would kindly ask you to look at the date, the 16th of June, 1995, at 9.30. Do you know where was the 102nd Muslim Brigade deployed at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not off the top of my head. If it is specified in the document, then my memory will be jogged, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read. It says: "Our forces knew information," this is 2.1, "or our forces were in combat-readiness, they were at the ready and at the starting position at the envisaged time. And at 0436 hours, the attack was launched along the axes ..." which are all enumerated. Please look, what rounds they used. I'm referring to bigger-sized calibre. My calculation is that they fired 549 shells without [as interpreted] 12.7, which should have also been banned. Could you please read this. 60-millimetre shells, 34; 82-millimetre shells, 63; 120-millimetre shells, nine; 12.7-millimetre rounds, 810 - I did not take that into my calculation; 105-millimetre shells, seven; M-57 RB, 11, and so on and so forth. What is this NG rounds, 20 of them were used?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be -- I don't know what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this nitroglycerin?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Possibly. It may be nitroglycerin. What can you tell us, how many brigades of this kind existed within the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The city of Sarajevo -- I don't know how many brigades did the 1st Corps have. It must have had at least three-plus brigades. I believe that it had more than three brigades. In any case, judging by this document, they were really well equipped and they were very active. You can see that this was their attack, this was their assault. It was an operation that was carried out in 1995 in the month of June and it was intending to break through from the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic -- yes, Mr. Tieger, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2415, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much more do you have for your re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two more documents, very briefly, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have a couple of matters to deal with at the end of today's session, but let's continue. Let's see how it evolves.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D20059.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the position of Fikret Prevljak in 1995, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D20059. Can this be blown up a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this document issued on the 16th of June at 10.00? The year is 1995.

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "Between 0700 and 1000 hours, our newly reached lines of defence on elevation 625, Lalovici, on the lines of Zlatiste, Sucura Kuca above Hladivode, and elevation 830 were exposed to constant and fierce artillery, tank and mortar fire from weapons of all calibre. There were intermittent combined artillery and infantry attacks on the above-mentioned lines in half-hour intervals. "The newly reached lines on elevation 830 and elevation 625 and in the sector of Zlatiste were integrated and the unit from the Sucura Kuca line withdrew to its initial position at 0810 hours because of fierce artillery fire. At the firing position in the sector of Tesanovo hill, we destroyed a tank with a TF-8 projectile at 0950." Can you please tell us what was going on from 7.00 in the morning to 10.00 in the morning? Who was acting, who was reacting?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, on that day in June, an attack was launched on all the defence lines of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, both from the inner ring as well as the outer ring, in co-ordination of the 1st Corps and the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And during the initial period of that operation, the Muslim forces had certain successes on all the front lines, starting with the southern front line as well as the northern and the north-western part of the front line. Certain positions were broken through; however, we rapidly consolidated our forces, we received artillery support, we managed to return them to their initial positions. Some of those positions took days to be reclaimed and that defensive lasted for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us where did the Serbian shells fall and could they be seen from the town? Those that fell on Zlatiste and Sucura Kuca.

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean when you say "Serbian shells."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When we attempted to return positions and the artillery fire on our trenches that they had taken over, could that be seen from the city?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe from the opposite side. Those shells were falling on the forward line, i.e., on the deployment of the Muslim forces which were engaged in attack in order to return to their initial positions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, and I am on to my last document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not to the document in the abstract, which appears to be authentic in the sense we've been using them, but I was waiting for some kind of relevance to the cross-examination to appear in the course of the questions and answers, and I think we're on a document admission exercise that is using unnecessary time and a bar table submission would appear to be more appropriate for matters like this. I don't see how this arises from the cross that was -- with this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whatever the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We almost adjourned. They say it's okay now. There has been a technical difficulty which has been now resolved. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Tieger asked about the number of shells and about where the shells fell and where they were falling. I wanted to ask the witness where the fierce fighting was going on, could the Serbian shells be seen from the city and could anybody actually ascribe them to the Serbian side. I was interested where they were falling and whether they could be discerned from the city itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that we have a basis to admit this. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2416, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we go for a further five minutes? I'm asking the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one last document and one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 23920.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, i.e., General Milosevic, which is what you see on the second page, under 2 it says: "I forbid arbitrary and uncontrolled opening of fire. Fire is to be opened only at useful targets - live targets, i.e., such targets which serve to inflict real losses on the enemy and does not represent 'attempts of intimidation.'" Colonel, sir, how does this tally with what you know about the tactics of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the attitude towards the city?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, you can see from Article 2, which is part of the corps command -- commander order, that only military targets should be fired upon in order to achieve effects, i.e., to achieve losses on the enemy side which is why fire is opened in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- Colonel, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having come to testify.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And of course, this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit D2417. Just before we adjourn, Mr. Tieger, the Chamber is seized of the Defence motion for image distortion of -- for witness Trifunovic, so I wonder whether we can have your response by tomorrow so that we can issue the decision before witness comes. I will deal with the remainder thing -- remaining thing tomorrow morning. So, Mr. Simic, that concludes your evidence and I -- on behalf of the Tribunal, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will rise all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.25 p.m.,
